主要内容: On July 8, 2015, Coty Inc. and The Procter & Gamble Company entered into a Transaction Agreement to merge P&G’s fine fragrance, color cosmetics, and hair color businesses into a subsidiary of Coty through a tax-free Reverse Morris Trust transaction. The deal was based on a proposal valuing the P&G Beauty Business at approximately $12.5 billion. Following the transaction, P&G shareholders would own 52% of the combined company, while Coty’s existing shareholders would own 48%. The transaction could be structured as a split-off or spin-off, with P&G shareholders potentially participating in an exchange offer for shares of a newly formed company comprising the P&G Beauty Business. The text describes a merger between a company and a subsidiary of P&G, where P&G shareholders will receive shares of the company in exchange for their shares of SplitCo. This Reverse Morris Trust transaction has been approved by the boards of both companies and by JAB Cosmetics B.V., which holds a majority of the combined voting power of the company’s common stock. JAB, the owner of all of the outstanding shares of the company’s Class B common stock representing approximately 97% of the company’s voting power, has granted shareholder consent and agreed to convert all such shares into Class A common stock. Following the conversion, the company’s common stock will consist of a single class, with JAB remaining the largest individual shareholder, owning approximately 33% of the fully diluted shares. The transaction is valued at $12.5 billion for the P&G Beauty Business, with the equity component valued at approximately $9.6 billion. The remaining consideration of $2.9 billion in assumed debt is subject to a $1 billion adjustment based on the company’s stock price. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2016, subject to regulatory clearances and other conditions.
